Elena Gomez: Heads-up: Enterprise retailer asked for a "spike-shield" capability — very short lived (15s-3m) ephemeral reservations that improve success during traffic spikes without consuming long-term reserved quota. They want clear fallthrough semantics and minimal billing surprises.
Ravi Menon: Clarify billing model: free tier of N shields/month, then per-shield overage? Or charge by duration/requests?
Elena Gomez: Customer prefers a free bucket (e.g., 300 shields/month) + per-shield overage after. They emphasized zero 429s during checkout bursts.
Diego Torres: Implementation idea: ephemeral lease object at admission with TTL. Lease consumes a tiny soft slot on a reserved pool node and carries a priority flag so scheduler prefers serving it. If lease cannot be allocated -> execute fallback sequence.
Katherine Wu: Fallback ordering? Current options: shared dedicated lane -> spot -> queue/429. For checkout we should avoid queueing; prefer degrade to a smaller model or lower parallelism.
Ravi Menon: Autoscale coupling question: are ephemeral leases allowed to trigger scale-up? Dangerous — could cause autoscale oscillation from flash events. Suggest leases are visible to autoscaler as a short-lived signal but we cap its contribution and require sustained usage to actually scale up.
Diego Torres: Agree. Architect note: add ephemeral signal to autoscale estimator with decay window (e.g., 90s). Also add global per-region shield cap to avoid hot partitions.
Katherine Wu: SLO/marketing phrasing: we shouldn't call it "guaranteed". Propose name: "spike-shield (soft reserve)" and document p95 success rate target for shield hits in pilot.
Elena Gomez: Product launch criteria draft: 1) pass synthetic checkout spike test (1000 reqs/sec for 30s) with <0.5% failures for shield-eligible requests; 2) Console shows shield consumption and remaining free bucket; 3) Billing emits overage events and invoice preview; 4) Pilot with 3 customers for 4 weeks.
Ravi Menon: Test harness: need a simulator that can create shield leases at scale and verify fallback paths. Also need integration tests asserting no more than X additional latency at p95 for reserved customers.
Diego Torres: Dev breakdown: a) admission lease allocator + TTL b) scheduler priority flag + node accounting c) autoscale estimator hook with capped ephemeral weight d) console telemetry + overage billing event e) e2e simulator and chaos tests. Rough estimate: 6 eng-weeks infra + 2 eng-weeks console + 2 qa-weeks.
Katherine Wu: Prioritization: Customer wants pilot in 4 weeks, but we have prewarm infra sprint ongoing. Recommend scoped MVP to meet timeline: implement admission + fallback ordering + telemetry + billing event (no autoscale coupling for MVP). That reduces to ~3 infra-weeks and 1 console-week.
Elena Gomez: MVP acceptance checklist: admission API/flag implemented; TTL leases enforceable; fallback order deterministic and documented; console shows live meter; pilot customers onboarded; overage billing validated.
Ravi Menon: Known risks: 1) hot-spotting on particular nodes due to lease packing; 2) opaque failure reasons for customers when shield not granted; 3) unexpected billing disputes. Mitigations: add anti-affinity packing rule, expand diagnostics in API response for why shield failed, and legal-approved billing language + reconciliation tool.
Diego Torres: Ops runbook items: automated detection rule for abnormal shield churn, emergency disable knob per-customer, and graceful drain that migrates active TTL leases to fallback lanes.
Katherine Wu: Also add a small UX flow for customers to opt-in/out of shield and set overage thresholds. For pilot, SE should handle opt-in to avoid accidental charges.
Elena Gomez: Action items: Ravi -> simulator spec + perf targets by Thu; Diego -> prototype lease allocator branch by next Tue (branch: feat/spike-shield); Katherine -> billing wording draft + console mockups by Fri; OpsBot: scheduled reminder to run shield chaos sim on 1777779000.
Elena Gomez: I'll update the Dedicated roadmap item and mark as "pilot candidate". Will coordinate SEs for customer onboarding. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
